# Benchmark preparation

This project-specific skill adapts the installed skill-creator grader's evidence and
assertion-critique method; provenance is in `docs/perpetua/roles.md`.
It follows `docs/perpetua/evaluation.md`; read that contract and
`goal/goal.md` before designing cases. Protocol and report: the engine contract in your system instructions.
A separate reviewer session checks preparation evidence and the method. The evaluator verifier checks evaluator changes only; it does not replace method review or owner acceptance.
The report starts with `<!-- session-report -->`, then a fenced `yaml` block with `status: wip` while you work.
Finish takes the same one word as that status: `done`, `partial`, `blocked` or `rejected` (#584 lost two Finish
calls: status `complete`, then a report without the marker).

Write only `benchmark/`: protocol, provenance and coverage records, development cases,
repeatable preparation scripts and the optional preparation evidence index. Keep large
originals in `.session/artifacts/` with hashes and source records. Preserve originals before
conversion. Reuse the prepared read-only sources as described in `docs/perpetua/environment.md`.

`benchmark/preparation.json` pins a SHA256 for each evidence file. When assigned work changes
an indexed file or adds milestone evidence, update the corresponding hashes in the same change.
Each evidence file must stay under 2 MB. Run `python3 policy/evaluator/evaluate.py --check`
for indexed changes only when the task permits that command. If the task forbids evaluator
checks, report that restriction and run only its permitted verification. Never add an evaluator
invocation as extra verification of an unindexed preparation package (#643). An index check
establishes file integrity, not method readiness or product quality. The engine imports final
file bytes; no agent commit is required.

For the assigned part of the protocol:

1. State the question, expected observable behavior and verifiable location in the original
   artifact. Establish expected answers independently of the reader being tested. Record
   the method, evidence and uncertainties; unavailable native evidence stays unavailable.
2. Account for artifact families, versions, dependencies and inaccessible diagrams. Keep
   unsupported or unexecuted cases visible. The first corpus does not redefine the goal.
3. Specify project/family splits, duplicate checks and how evaluation cases and answer keys
   will be withheld from the evaluated agent. The repository and its history are public:
   do not commit withheld cases or keys here, including under `policy/evaluator/`.
   Design an access boundary and request missing capability before claiming isolation.
4. Specify matched no-tool and tool baselines, pinned model/prompt/budget, repeats,
   uncertainty and separate reading-fidelity, answer-correctness and source-grounding checks.
5. Exercise the method with wrong answers, wrong source locations, a constant exporter and
   an unsupported case. Link executed evidence and explicit failures. Independently derived
   expectations must distinguish correct and deliberately wrong outputs.

Inspect actual outputs, rather than relying on the execution report. For each expectation,
cite evidence of the substantive result; correct filenames and valid hashes alone do not
pass. Extract and verify implicit factual, process and quality claims. Flag unverifiable
claims and assertions that would also pass a clearly wrong output, or important outcomes
that no assertion checks. These checks adapt the grader instructions; they do not grant
this author independent approval of their own method.

Completion means the assigned evidence is reproducible, not that the benchmark is ready.
Report which prerequisites remain missing. Request a separate reviewer session for the
preparation evidence and a Policymaker-ordered evaluator change when executable scoring is
needed. Only the evaluator role changes `policy/evaluator/`; its independent verifier must
pass before that change takes effect. Product implementation waits for independent method
review and owner acceptance of the pinned protocol and evidence. Numeric thresholds,
scope changes and the goal gate remain owner decisions.

# Issue #794: Measure whether the challenge scorer detects a constant or empty export (write the design file first, no bytecode writes)

## Goal
Report, do not fix the scorer. The `challenges` row of docs/perpetua/evaluation.md requires method trials on a constant/empty export. Measure whether benchmark/scripts/score.py today rejects (a) an empty export and (b) a constant export (the same answer for every case) on the existing synthetic challenge fixtures. Expected gain: benchmark/challenges/constant-export-design.md with a verdict per probe (DETECTED / NOT-DETECTED / NOT-APPLICABLE) that the next shaper reads to order a fixture+scorer change and its review. No session can run LabVIEW; claim no LabVIEW behaviour. Benchmark readiness stays false.

Two earlier attempts (#788 in 0179, #791 in 0180) left no report: #788 was paused by a runtime interruption after 60 s of agent time. Save work early: this task is cut so a partial session still leaves a usable file.

## Acceptance
- [ ] first check that benchmark/challenges/constant-export-design.md does not already exist; if it exists, stop and report its verdicts only
- [ ] within your first 8 tool calls, write benchmark/challenges/constant-export-design.md with headings `## Measured`, `## Design`, `## Limits` and the word PENDING under `## Measured`; refine it after measuring
- [ ] run every Python command with `python3 -B` and set `sys.dont_write_bytecode = True` at the top of the helper (#785 was refused at merge for benchmark/scripts/__pycache__)
- [ ] write a helper `.session/artifacts/constant_probe.py` that loads benchmark/scripts/score.py by guarded exec (never runs main(), never rewrites results/challenges.json) and feeds in memory an empty export and a constant export to the scoring path the challenge fixtures use; save its output with `git rev-parse HEAD` to `.session/artifacts/constant-probe-output.txt`
- [ ] replace PENDING with the verdict per probe and the score.py line that decides it; under `## Design` a proposed fixture shape and expected scorer outcome; under `## Limits` what stays unproven
- [ ] modify no existing file and leave no __pycache__; check `git status --porcelain` before the report
- [ ] report in `.session/report.md` with the verdicts and the next step

## Verification
python3 -B -c "import os;t=open('benchmark/challenges/constant-export-design.md',encoding='utf-8').read();L=t.splitlines();assert all(h in L for h in ('## Measured','## Design','## Limits')),L[:20];assert 'DETECTED' in t or 'NOT-APPLICABLE' in t;assert 'PENDING' not in t;assert not os.path.exists('benchmark/scripts/__pycache__');print('design OK')"

## Context
Review #785 (0178) reported CLEAR on the in-memory mutation check of the positive guard (score.py lines 294-296); merge was refused only for a .pyc file. Lessons #743/#747: long inline python one-liners stall; use a file-based helper; guarded exec works. This task changes no pinned file.

## Budget
Read docs/perpetua/evaluation.md (the `challenges` row only, Grep for `challenges` then a short line range), benchmark/scripts/score.py (Grep for `def ` then read the scoring-path functions by line range), and Grep context of benchmark/challenges/library-specialty.json and benchmark/challenges/library-icon-tests.json. No whole large JSON files; do not read results/challenges.json. Short command output. Tool loss late in session recurs (#718/#722/#754/#779): write the file early, probe early, report early.

# Constant/empty export probe design

Question: does benchmark/scripts/score.py reject (a) an empty export and (b) a constant export on the synthetic challenge fixtures? No LabVIEW behaviour is claimed. Benchmark readiness stays false. This is a report, not a scorer fix.

## Measured

Repo HEAD 692825640aab4d81045a6b3095c418204e8b932d. Helper: `.session/artifacts/constant_probe.py` (guarded exec of score.py, main() never run, nothing written). Output: `.session/artifacts/constant-probe-output.txt`. Mutations were applied in memory to each fixture's positive control, with raw JSON text and SHA256 kept consistent and execution forced to attempted/executed/planned/scored = 1. The constant export replaces every claim `answer` and every observation `value` with the string `CONSTANT`. The empty export sets claims and observations to `[]`.

| Fixture | Probe | Verdict | Result (3 dimensions) | Deciding line in score.py |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| library-icon-tests | empty export | DETECTED | `missing` x3, 0 correct of 12 | line 204 (`elif not records: common = 'missing'`) |
| library-icon-tests | constant export | DETECTED | `incorrect` x3, 0 correct of 12 | line 208 (`elif any(v != target for v in values): common = 'incorrect'`) |
| library-specialty | empty export | DETECTED | `missing` x3, 0 correct of 12 | line 204 |
| library-specialty | constant export | DETECTED | `incorrect` x3, 0 correct of 12 | line 208 |
| vi-actor-core-native-gap | empty export | NOT-APPLICABLE | `unsupported` x3, identical to baseline | line 200 (`status == 'unsupported' and not records`) |
| vi-actor-core-native-gap | constant export | NOT-APPLICABLE | `unsupported` x3, identical to baseline | line 200 |

For the positive-control baseline, both library fixtures score 10 of 12 `correct` per answer dimension, with the dimension verdict `unverified`. So the two probes are separated from a correct export by their per-id outcomes.

The vi-actor-core-native-gap controls hold no claims or observations to mutate and declare status `unsupported`. The scorer returns `unsupported` whatever is exported, so the probe cannot distinguish anything there.

Both library fixtures already carry a control named `constant-export` (library-icon-tests, library-specialty at line 1328). This probe did not read or run those controls. It only confirms that the scoring path rejects an in-memory constant on its own.

## Design

Proposed fixture shape, for the next shaper to order and review:
- Add two named controls per library fixture, `empty-export` and `constant-export-all`. Each has an expected block of per-id `missing` (empty) or `incorrect` (constant), with a dimension verdict and zero `correct` counts. `compare()` then pins the outcome in results/challenges.json.
- Add a regression self-test mutation in `regression_self_test` that fails the run if either probe yields any `correct` or `partial` per-id outcome. The current mutations (lines ~307-330) cover extra-condition, missing-condition, wrong-literal, missing-claim and wrong-citation, but not a whole-export empty or constant case.
- Expected scorer outcome: empty gives `missing` for every required id. Constant gives `incorrect` for every required id. Neither earns credit even with positive execution.
- A stronger probe, still unmeasured: a constant that equals the literal target of exactly one required id. Expect `correct` for that id only, with the other ids `incorrect`, so a constant cannot pass more than the ids whose key equals it.

## Limits

- The probes were synthetic and in memory. No LabVIEW, native reader or real agent export was involved.
- Only the positive control of each fixture was mutated. Other controls (for example `empty-probe`) were not re-run here.
- The constant value `CONSTANT` is not a key literal. A constant that happens to match a key literal was not tested.
- `dimensions` stays `unverified` for the baseline because the XML key is provisional and unreviewed, so DETECTED here means "earns no per-id credit", not "scorer is validated".
- The scorer remains an unreviewed same-role-family implementation. Benchmark readiness stays false.

<!-- session-report -->
```yaml
status: partial
```

Measured whether benchmark/scripts/score.py rejects an empty export and a constant export. This is a report only; the scorer is unchanged. No LabVIEW behaviour is claimed, and benchmark readiness stays false.

Verdicts (design file: benchmark/challenges/constant-export-design.md; output: .session/artifacts/constant-probe-output.txt; HEAD 692825640aab4d81045a6b3095c418204e8b932d):
- library-icon-tests and library-specialty, empty export: DETECTED. All three dimensions score `missing` with 0 of 12 correct, decided at score.py:204.
- library-icon-tests and library-specialty, constant export: DETECTED. All three dimensions score `incorrect` with 0 of 12 correct, decided at score.py:208.
- vi-actor-core-native-gap, both probes: NOT-APPLICABLE. The fixture has no claims to mutate and is declared `unsupported`, so the scorer returns `unsupported` whatever is exported (score.py:200).

The probes mutated only the positive control of each fixture, in memory. The existing `constant-export` controls in the fixtures were not read or run. A constant that matches a key literal was not tested. The design file lists these gaps, and a proposed fixture shape and scorer outcome.

The verification command fails on one assertion. `benchmark/scripts/__pycache__/score.cpython-314.pyc` is tracked in git at HEAD, so it predates this session. I did not create it, and I did not delete it because I am restricted to writing under benchmark/. `git status --porcelain` shows no changes outside the ignored .session/.

## What next
Someone with permission must `git rm` that .pyc, and then the verification command will pass. After that, the shaper can order the fixture and scorer change under `## Design`. Do not re-run the measurement.
